changed: Windows: POST /export with format=glb now calls EXPORT_API->ExportGLB() instead of EXPORT_API->ExportGLTF(path, options, true). Verified by hand (curl + pygltflib) that the old code produced JSON glTF with base64-embedded buffers regardless of the bGLBinary flag - not actually binary .glb - despite reporting success. ExportGLB is the SDK's dedicated binary-GLB function (CLO_SDK/Samples/ExportPlugin/ExportPlugin.cpp's ExportGLB_Sample()), matching what CLO's own File > Export > glTF 2.0 (GLB) menu produces. format=gltf (non-GLB) path still uses ExportGLTF, now explicitly passing bGLBinary=false to match the SDK sample's own usage.

Windows: export options.scale changed from 1.0f to 0.001f, matching the SDK's own documented default ('use 0.001 for gltf in default' - CLO's internal unit is millimeters, gltf/glb expect meters). The old value would have produced exports 1000x the intended size.

Windows: removed the options.bEmbedded = asGLB assignment on the export options struct - not set in either official SDK sample (ExportGLTF_Sample, ExportGLB_Sample); left at its SDK default instead of being driven off the GLB/GLTF format choice.
fixed: Windows: /export format=glb was silently producing invalid (non-binary) output while reporting success=true. Root cause: wrong SDK function called (ExportGLTF's bGLBinary bool does not select true binary output; ExportGLB is a separate, dedicated function). See Mirra plan doc .agent/website-launch/01-docker-and-clo-render-pipeline.md, Phase 2 findings, for the full investigation.
known_issues: POST /export hangs indefinitely when called against a completely empty CLO scene (no avatar, no patterns loaded) - queue never drains, CLO's main thread visibly consumes CPU but never returns. Not yet root-caused; not a blocker since the real pipeline use case always has an avatar loaded first. Recovery requires restarting CLO3D.

This fix (ExportGLB vs ExportGLTF) has only been verified on Windows against an avatar-only scene (no garment/patterns loaded). Not yet verified with a garment loaded (the Step 3 VTO use case) - step_12_texture_glb.py may need its pygltflib load call adjusted too if any further format quirks surface there.
Mac not ported yet - still calling the old ExportGLTF path. Deliberately deferred (Windows-only focus per current plan).

notes: Fix found via live testing: manually exporting through CLO's own UI (File > Export > glTF 2.0 (GLB)) produced a valid binary .glb (verified with pygltflib - correct 'glTF' binary magic header, loaded cleanly), while the plugin's REST /export endpoint on the same scene produced JSON-embedded content mislabeled as .glb. Cross-referenced against the CLO SDK's own headers/samples (CLOAPIInterface/include/ExportAPIInterface.h, Samples/ExportPlugin/ExportPlugin.cpp) to find the correct function. Needs rebuild + manual install (Administrator) + CLO restart + re-verification before use.
